# Auto-generated Supabase types

`supabase.ts` is generated by `npm run gen:types` and reflects the live
public schema of the linked Supabase project.

## First-time setup (one-shot per machine)

```bash
# 1) Get a personal access token from
#    https://supabase.com/dashboard/account/tokens
# 2) Export it for the current shell
export SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN=sbp_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

# 3) Link this repo to the project (creates ./supabase/ config)
npm run db:link

# 4) Generate types
npm run gen:types
```

## Refreshing types after a schema change

```bash
npm run gen:types
git diff types/supabase.ts   # review the diff
git add types/supabase.ts && git commit -m "Regenerate Supabase types"
```

Yes, the generated file is committed (not gitignored). Vercel builds
need the type definitions and `gen:types` requires a personal token —
shipping the file makes builds reproducible.

## Why this exists

`src/lib/supabase.ts` previously hand-rolled a `Database` type that only
covered 4 tables (`forwarders`, `shipping_rates`, `centers`,
`member_grade_definitions`). The actual schema has dozens more
(`jimscanner_blog_*`, `jimscanner_trends_*`, `jimscanner_gsc_*`,
`exchange_rates`, `admin_actions`, ...). Most queries used string table
names and lost type safety. Auto-generated types fix that.

See `memory/strategic_pivot_2026_05_09.md` (E1).
